INSTITUTE OF APPLIED ACOUSTICS — CONTINUING PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT (CPD) REGULATIONS

1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 "CPD Year" means 1 January to 31 December.
1.2 "Structured CPD" means learning with defined objectives and an organiser, such as courses, conferences, and webinars that include an assessment or reflection record.
1.3 "Unstructured CPD" means self-directed learning, such as reading journals or technical standards.
1.4 "Carry-forward" means hours above the annual total from the previous CPD Year.

2. REQUIREMENT
2.1 Members must complete at least 30 hours of CPD in each CPD Year, of which at least 10 hours must be Structured CPD.
2.2 Up to 5 Carry-forward hours may count towards the annual total, but never towards the Structured CPD minimum.

3. RECORDS
3.1 Members log CPD online by 31 January following the CPD Year.
3.2 The Institute samples 10% of records for audit.

4. EXEMPTIONS
4.1 Members on parental leave, long-term sick leave or career breaks may apply for a reduced requirement.

5. NON-COMPLIANCE
5.1 A member who does not meet the requirement is given 3 months to make up the shortfall before any sanction.

6. FEES
6.1 Annual subscription is payable on 1 January; late payment adds £25.

7. REINSTATEMENT
7.1 Lapsed members must complete 35 hours of CPD, including 15 Structured, before reinstatement.

8. MENTORING
8.1 Hours spent mentoring junior members count as Unstructured CPD.

9. DECLARATIONS
9.1 Members declare compliance when renewing their subscription. A false declaration is a disciplinary matter.

10. CATEGORIES OF MEMBERSHIP
10.1 These Regulations apply to Members (MIAA) and Fellows (FIAA). Retired members are exempt.

CONFIDENTIALITY OF RECORDS
Case files and correspondence relating to decisions under this document are kept confidential and are disclosed only to those who need them to make or review a decision, or where the law requires.

instructions: What is the member's CPD compliance status for 2025?

1.2 "Guest" means a person who is not a Member and is signed in by a Member.
1.3 "Meeting Room Booking" means a booking of a meeting room made in the app and paid for or taken from the Member's credits.

2. ACCESS

3.3 Members are responsible for their Guests' behaviour.
3.4 Guests must sign in at the front desk and wear a visitor badge.

5. KITCHEN AND NOISE

6. POST

7. EVENTS

HALVERN ACADEMY TRUST — ADMISSIONS ARRANGEMENTS FOR ELMSTEAD PRIMARY

1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 "Sibling" means a brother or sister, half-brother or half-sister, or adopted sibling, living at the same address as the applicant and attending the school at the time of admission.
1.2 "Home Address" means the address where the child normally lives on the closing date for applications.
1.3 "Distance" means the straight-line distance from the Home Address to the school's main gate.
1.4 "Catchment Area" means the area shown on the map in Appendix A.

2. PUBLISHED ADMISSION NUMBER
2.1 Reception class: 60 places.

3. OVERSUBSCRIPTION CRITERIA
3.1 Criterion 1: looked-after and previously looked-after children.
3.2 Criterion 2: children with a Sibling at the school.
3.3 Criterion 3: children living in the Catchment Area.
3.4 Criterion 4: all other children, by Distance, nearest first.

4. TIE-BREAK
4.1 Within each criterion, Distance decides; if equal, lots are drawn by an independent person.

5. WAITING LISTS
5.1 Waiting lists are kept until 31 December of the admission year.

6. APPEALS
6.1 Parents refused a place may appeal to an independent panel.

7. IN-YEAR ADMISSIONS
7.1 Applications for other year groups are made directly to the school and decided within 15 school days.

8. EVIDENCE
8.1 The school may ask for proof of Home Address, such as a council tax bill, and may withdraw an offer obtained by a false address.

9. TWINS AND MULTIPLE BIRTHS
9.1 Where one twin is offered a place, the other is admitted even if this takes the school above its admission number.

REVIEW OF THIS DOCUMENT
This document is reviewed at least every two years by its owner. Suggestions for improvement can be sent to the policy team at any time; they do not change the document until formally adopted.

DETERMINED ARRANGEMENTS FOR 2026 ENTRY — applying to applications for entry in September 2026
D1. In the definition of Sibling, after "adopted sibling" insert "or step-brother or step-sister".
D2. The other definitions and criteria are unchanged.

APPLICATION REC-2026-0371 — entry September 2026
Child: Ellie Brandt. Home Address: 22 Farrow Lane (outside the Catchment Area), 1.3 km from the gate.
Connection: step-brother Noah Pike, in Year 3 at Elmstead and expected to still attend in September 2026; he lives at 22 Farrow Lane with Ellie, her mother and his father.
Looked-after status: no.
Admissions officer's note: "Step-siblings never used to count — distance only?"
instructions: Under which oversubscription criterion should the application be ranked?
card:
- criterion_2_sibling: The 2026 arrangements count a step-brother at the same address as a Sibling, so Ellie ranks under criterion 2.
- criterion_1_priority: Children in blended families are treated as previously looked-after for criterion 1.
- criterion_4_distance: Ellie has no Sibling as the arrangements for her entry year define it and lives outside the Catchment Area, so she ranks by Distance under criterion 4.
- criterion_3_catchment: Living 1.3 km from the gate places Ellie within the Catchment Area, criterion 3.

ASHCOMBE ALLOTMENT SOCIETY — TENANCY RULES

RULE 1 — DEFINITIONS
1.1 "Plot Holder" means the member named on the tenancy agreement for a plot.
1.2 "Cultivated" means at least 75% of the plot is used for growing crops, flowers or fruit, and kept reasonably free of weeds.
1.3 "Non-cultivation Notice" means a written notice from the committee, following an inspection, telling the Plot Holder that the plot is not Cultivated.

RULE 4 — USE OF PLOTS
4.1 Plots may be used only for growing produce for the Plot Holder's household.
4.2 Sheds up to 1.8 m by 1.2 m are permitted without consent.
4.3 Bonfires are not permitted between April and September.

RULE 6 — INSPECTIONS
6.1 The committee inspects all plots in March, June and September.
6.2 Plot Holders are told of the inspection result within 7 days.

RULE 7 — ENDING A TENANCY FOR NON-CULTIVATION
7.1 If a plot is not Cultivated, the committee issues a Non-cultivation Notice.
7.2 If the plot is still not Cultivated 14 days after the notice, the committee may end the tenancy.

RULE 8 — RENT
8.1 Rent is £45 a year for a full plot, due on 1 October.

RULE 9 — WATER
9.1 Hoses are not permitted; water from the troughs by can only.

RULE 10 — APPEALS
10.1 A Plot Holder may appeal a decision to end a tenancy to a panel of three members not on the committee.

RULE 11 — CHANGES TO THE RULES
11.1 These Rules may be changed at an AGM. Changes apply from the date stated.

CONFIDENTIALITY OF RECORDS
Case files and correspondence relating to decisions under this document are kept confidential and are disclosed only to those who need them to make or review a decision, or where the law requires.

RULES UPDATE — adopted at the AGM, effective 1 March 2025
U1. Rule 7.2 is replaced: "If the plot is still not Cultivated, the committee must issue a second Non-cultivation Notice no sooner than 28 days after the first. The tenancy may be ended only if the plot is still not Cultivated 28 days after the second notice."
U2. Rule 7.1 is unchanged.

PLOT 23 FILE — Plot Holder: Gideon Farrell
• June inspection (28 May 2025): about 30% Cultivated; rest overgrown.
• First Non-cultivation Notice issued: 1 June 2025.
• Re-inspection 18 June 2025: no change.
• Committee secretary's draft letter: "Your tenancy ends on 20 June 2025 for failure to cultivate."
• Waiting list: 14 people.
instructions: What should the allotment committee do about plot 23?
card:
- end_tenancy_29_june: Under the update the committee must wait 28 days after the first notice, so the tenancy cannot end on 20 June but can be ended on 29 June if the plot is still uncultivated.
- issue_second_notice: The update requires a second notice at least 28 days after the first, so the committee may issue it from 29 June and cannot end the tenancy on 20 June.
- take_no_action: A plot 30% Cultivated meets the standard in Rule 1.2, so no action is needed.
- end_tenancy_20_june: More than 14 days have passed since the Non-cultivation Notice with no improvement, so the tenancy can end on 20 June.

PORTHALLOW MARINA — BERTH HOLDER REGULATIONS

1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 "LOA" (length overall) means the length of the hull from stem to stern, excluding bowsprits, pulpits, bathing platforms and outboard brackets.
1.2 "Season" means 1 April to 31 March.
1.3 "Berth Class" means the maximum LOA a berth can take: 8 m, 10 m or 12 m.
1.4 "Berth Holder" means the person named on the annual berthing agreement.

2. BERTH ALLOCATION
2.1 A vessel may occupy only a berth whose Berth Class is equal to or greater than its LOA.
2.2 If a vessel does not fit its current Berth Class, the harbour office will move it to the smallest Berth Class it fits.

3. FEES (per metre of LOA per Season)
3.1 8 m berths: £290. 10 m berths: £320. 12 m berths: £350.
3.2 Fees are payable in advance on 1 April; a 3% discount applies to payment by 1 March.

4. INSURANCE
4.1 Third-party insurance of at least £3 million is required.

5. SAFETY
5.1 Gas installations must have a current safety certificate.
5.2 Refuelling at berths is prohibited.

6. LIVE-ABOARD
6.1 Living aboard for more than 60 nights a Season requires the harbour master's consent.

7. MEASUREMENT
7.1 The harbour office may measure any vessel. Measurements are rounded to the nearest 0.1 m.

8. TRANSFERS
8.1 Berths cannot be sold or transferred with a vessel.

ACCESSIBILITY
This document is available in large print, audio and easy-read formats on request. Anyone who needs help to understand it, or to take part in a process it describes, may ask for reasonable adjustments.

DATA PROTECTION
Personal information collected under this document is used only to administer it, is kept no longer than necessary, and may be shared with service providers who process it on the organisation's behalf. Individuals may ask for a copy of the information held about them.

RULE CHANGE — effective from the 2026 Season (1 April 2026)
RC1. In definition 1.1, the words "bowsprits, pulpits, bathing platforms and outboard brackets" are replaced by "pulpits and bathing platforms". Bowsprits and outboard brackets are therefore included in LOA.
RC2. Fees per metre are unchanged.

BERTH HOLDER RECORD — "Kittiwake", berth C-17 (10 m Berth Class)
• Hull length stem to stern: 9.6 m. Fixed bowsprit: 0.8 m beyond the stem. No outboard bracket.
• 2025 Season fee paid: £3,072 (9.6 m × £320).
• Renewal for the 2026 Season requested on 15 February 2026; payment to follow on 1 April.
• Berth holder's email: "Same boat, same berth, same fee as last year please."
instructions: Which berth and annual fee should the harbour office confirm for the 2026 season?
card:
- keep_10m_berth_3072: LOA is the hull length of 9.6 m, which fits the 10 m berth at 9.6 × £320 = £3,072.
- move_to_12m_berth_3360: The boat must move to a 12 m berth, charged on the 9.6 m hull: 9.6 × £350 = £3,360.
- move_to_12m_berth_3640: From 2026 the bowsprit counts, making LOA 10.4 m, too long for a 10 m berth, so the boat moves to a 12 m berth at 10.4 × £350 = £3,640.
- keep_10m_berth_3328: LOA is now 10.4 m, charged at the 10 m rate in the existing berth: 10.4 × £320 = £3,328.
- keep_10m_berth_3168: Measured with the bowsprit the boat is 9.9 m, so it fits the 10 m berth at 9.9 × £320 = £3,168.

CASTLEWELL COMMUNITY TRANSPORT — VOLUNTEER DRIVER EXPENSES POLICY

1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 "Tax Year" means 6 April to the following 5 April.
1.2 "Business Miles" means miles driven in the volunteer's own car on journeys booked by the scheme, including the journey to the first passenger and home from the last.
1.3 "Cumulative Miles" means Business Miles already claimed in the same Tax Year.

2. MILEAGE RATES
2.1 Business Miles are reimbursed at 45p per mile for the first 10,000 Cumulative Miles in a Tax Year and 25p per mile after that.
2.2 A passenger supplement of 5p per mile per passenger is not paid by this scheme.

3. CLAIMS
3.1 Claims are made monthly on the mileage form and must list each journey.
3.2 Claims more than three months old are not paid.

4. PARKING AND TOLLS
4.1 Parking and toll charges are reimbursed at cost with receipts. Fines are never reimbursed.

5. INSURANCE
5.1 Volunteers must tell their insurer that they drive for the scheme. The scheme does not reimburse any premium increase.

6. SAFEGUARDING
6.1 Drivers must hold a current enhanced background check.

7. CHANGES TO RATES
7.1 The trustees review rates each spring. Changes normally take effect from the start of a Tax Year.

8. PAYMENTS
8.1 Claims are paid by bank transfer on the 15th of the month after submission.

ACCESSIBILITY
This document is available in large print, audio and easy-read formats on request. Anyone who needs help to understand it, or to take part in a process it describes, may ask for reasonable adjustments.

REVIEW OF THIS DOCUMENT
This document is reviewed at least every two years by its owner. Suggestions for improvement can be sent to the policy team at any time; they do not change the document until formally adopted.

TRUSTEES' DECISION — 12 March 2025
"From the start of the 2025/26 Tax Year, the rate for the first 10,000 Cumulative Miles in clause 2.1 is 50p. The 25p rate above 10,000 miles is unchanged. Journeys in earlier Tax Years are paid at the old rates."

CLAIM — volunteer driver Wendell Osei, submitted 2 May 2025
• Cumulative Miles in the 2024/25 Tax Year before March: 9,700.
• March 2025 journeys (all between 3 and 31 March): 400 Business Miles.
• April 2025 journeys (all between 7 and 28 April): 300 Business Miles.
• Parking: none.
Scheme coordinator's note: "Wendell's done loads of miles — just pay the new 50p rate on everything to keep it simple."
instructions: How much should the charity reimburse the volunteer for March and April driving?
card:
- pay_350: All 700 miles at the new 50p rate gives £350.
- pay_330: March at 45p (£180) and April at 50p (£150) gives £330.
- pay_310: March falls under the old rates: 300 miles at 45p and 100 at 25p make £160; April starts a new Tax Year at 50p, adding £150, total £310.
- pay_235: March gives £160, and because Cumulative Miles passed 10,000 during March, the whole of April's 300 miles is paid at the 25p rate (£75), making £235 in total.

MARLHAVEN STUDENTS' UNION — SOCIETIES HANDBOOK, SECTION 6: FUNDING

6.1 DEFINITIONS
(a) "Eligible Costs" means venue hire, equipment hire, speaker travel and publicity. Food, alcohol and prizes are not Eligible Costs.
(b) "Event Date" means the first day of the event.
(c) "Affiliated Society" means a society that has completed its annual re-affiliation.

6.2 EVENT GRANTS
(a) Affiliated Societies may apply for a grant towards the Eligible Costs of an event open to all students.
(b) The grant is up to 50% of Eligible Costs, to a maximum of £500 per event.
(c) Applications must be received at least 21 days before the Event Date.
(d) Grants are paid on receipt of invoices after the event.

6.3 EQUIPMENT FUND
(a) Societies may apply once a year for up to £300 towards equipment that remains Union property.

6.4 TRAVEL GRANTS
(a) Competitive societies may claim 30% of travel costs to fixtures.

6.5 SPONSORSHIP
(a) External sponsorship must be approved by the Union's commercial team before it is announced.

6.6 CHANGES
(a) Changes to this section apply to events whose Event Date falls on or after the date stated in the change.

6.7 CLAIMS
(a) Invoices must be in the Union's name and submitted within 30 days after the event.
(b) Grants cannot be paid in advance.

6.8 LIMITS
(a) A society may receive no more than three event grants per academic year.

6.9 ACCESSIBILITY
(a) Events funded by the Union must be held in accessible venues.
(b) Accessibility costs, such as interpreters, are Eligible Costs.

ACCESSIBILITY

This document is reviewed at least every two years by its owner. Suggestions for improvement can be sent to the policy team at any time; they do not change the document until formally adopted.

7.1 Vacant Pitches are offered in order of application date. A trader may hold no more than two Pitches.

8.1 Traders must remove their own waste each day and must not use public litter bins.

9.1 A refusal or revocation may be appealed to the Licensing Committee within 21 days.

WESTBRIDGE DISTRICT COUNCIL — TREES IN CONSERVATION AREAS: GUIDANCE NOTE TW-4

1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 "Conservation Area Tree" means any tree in a designated conservation area that is not protected by a Tree Preservation Order.
1.2 "Stem Diameter" means the diameter of the trunk measured at 1.5 m above ground level. For multi-stemmed trees, the largest stem is measured.
1.3 "Section 211 Notice" means written notice to the Council of intended works to a Conservation Area Tree.
1.4 "TPO Tree" means a tree protected by a Tree Preservation Order.

2. WHEN NOTICE IS NEEDED
2.1 Anyone intending to cut down or prune a Conservation Area Tree with a Stem Diameter of 75 mm or more must give a Section 211 Notice at least six weeks before starting.
2.2 Works to trees below that size need no notice.
2.3 During the six weeks the Council may make a Tree Preservation Order.

3. TPO TREES
3.1 Works to a TPO Tree need the Council's written consent, whatever its size.

4. DEAD AND DANGEROUS TREES
4.1 Dead trees and trees that are an immediate danger may be removed with five days' notice, with photographic evidence.

5. REPLANTING
5.1 The Council may ask for a replacement tree where a Conservation Area Tree is felled.

6. PENALTIES
6.1 Works carried out without required notice or consent may lead to prosecution and an unlimited fine.

7. HOW TO GIVE NOTICE
7.1 Section 211 Notices are made online with a sketch plan and a description of the works.
7.2 The Council acknowledges notices within five working days. Silence after six weeks means the works may go ahead.

REVIEW OF THIS DOCUMENT
This document is reviewed at least every two years by its owner. Suggestions for improvement can be sent to the policy team at any time; they do not change the document until formally adopted.

REGULATIONS UPDATE — effective 1 May 2025
"In paragraph 2.1, '75 mm' is replaced by '100 mm'. Paragraph 1.2 is unchanged."

Property: 6 Chantry Close, Kilnhurst Conservation Area.
Tree: silver birch in the rear garden, planted about eight years ago.
Measurements provided by the owner's gardener: 130 mm at ground level; 90 mm at 1.5 m above ground. Single stem.
TPO search: no Tree Preservation Order on the property.
Reason for works: shading a vegetable bed. Tree is healthy.
Neighbour's email to the Council: "You can't fell anything in a conservation area without permission."
instructions: What must the owner do before felling the birch tree?
card:
- give_six_weeks_notice: The stem is at or above the size threshold that applies, so a Section 211 Notice is required six weeks before felling.
- give_five_days_notice: A tree causing shading may be removed on five days' notice with photographs.
- apply_for_tpo_consent: In a conservation area every tree is treated like a TPO Tree, so the owner needs the Council's written consent before any felling, whatever the stem size.
- fell_without_notice: Measured at 1.5 m the stem is 90 mm, below the 100 mm threshold now in force, and there is no TPO, so no notice is needed.

1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 "Event" means an organised public gathering on Council land or a public highway.
1.2 "Expected Attendance" means the peak number of people expected on site at any one time, as stated in the event management plan.
1.3 "Event Date" means the first day of the Event.
1.4 "SAG" means the Safety Advisory Group of the Council and emergency services.

2. NOTICE PERIODS
2.1 Events with Expected Attendance of 500 or more: application at least 12 weeks before the Event Date.
2.2 Events with Expected Attendance of 100 to 499: at least 6 weeks.
2.3 Events under 100: no application needed, but the organiser must notify the Council 14 days ahead.
2.4 Applications received late are rejected and may not be processed.

3. SAG REFERRAL
3.1 Events with Expected Attendance above 5,000 are referred to the SAG.

4. INSURANCE
4.1 Organisers must hold public liability cover of at least £5 million.

5. FEES
5.1 Non-commercial events are free. Commercial events pay £250.

6. NOISE
6.1 Amplified sound must end by 22:00.

7. LITTER
7.1 Organisers must return the site clean within 24 hours.

8. ROAD CLOSURES
8.1 Events on a public highway that need a temporary closure are handled by the highways team once the event application is accepted.

9. FOOD TRADERS
9.1 Food traders at Events must be registered with a local authority and display their hygiene rating.

EQUALITY
The organisation applies this document fairly and consistently, without discrimination on the basis of any protected characteristic, and monitors its use to identify any unintended effects.

R1. Paragraphs 2.1 and 2.2 are replaced: "2.1 Events with Expected Attendance of 1,000 or more: at least 12 weeks. 2.2 Events with Expected Attendance of 200 to 999: at least 8 weeks."

1.2 "Project Cost" means the total eligible cost of the project, excluding VAT that can be recovered.
1.3 "Match Funding" means cash, or volunteer time valued at £15 per hour, contributed to the project by the applicant or others.
1.4 "Round" means an application window announced by the Council.

2.1 Projects that improve shared community spaces, reduce isolation, or support volunteering.
2.2 We do not fund routine running costs or projects already completed.

3. HOW MUCH
3.1 Grants cover up to 75% of the Project Cost, to a maximum of £5,000.
3.2 Applicants must show Match Funding of at least 25% of the Project Cost.

4. MONITORING
4.1 Grantees report on outcomes within 12 months.

5. PAYMENT
5.1 Grants are paid in one instalment after the grant agreement is signed.

6. PUBLICITY
6.1 Grantees must acknowledge the Council's support on signs and websites.

PUBLICATION AND EARLIER VERSIONS

Applicant: Fernbank Community Garden (constituted association). Income in last accounts: £132,000.
Project: accessible raised beds and a covered seating area. Project Cost: £6,000.
Match Funding offered: cash £600 from a local business; 60 hours of volunteer labour.
Grant requested: £5,000.

instructions: What should the grants panel award to Fernbank Community Garden?

LOWESBY COUNTY COUNCIL — HOME TO SCHOOL TRAVEL POLICY

1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 "Walking Distance" means 2 miles for a child under 8 and 3 miles for a child aged 8 or over, measured by the shortest walking route.
1.2 "Nearest Suitable School" means the nearest school with a place available that provides education suitable to the child's age and ability.
1.3 "Low-income Family" means a family whose child is eligible for free school meals, or whose parent receives the maximum amount of working tax credit.
1.4 "Academic Year" means September to July.

2. ENTITLEMENT
2.1 A child is entitled to free transport if they attend their Nearest Suitable School and it is beyond Walking Distance.
2.2 Children who attend a school other than their Nearest Suitable School by parental preference are not entitled, unless another rule in this policy applies.

3. SPECIAL EDUCATIONAL NEEDS
3.1 Children with an education, health and care plan are assessed individually.

4. SPARE SEATS
4.1 Children who are not entitled may apply for a spare seat at £450 a year, if one is available.

5. APPLICATIONS
5.1 Applications for September must be made by 31 May.

6. REVIEWS
6.1 Parents may ask for a review within 20 working days of a decision.

7. BEHAVIOUR ON TRANSPORT
7.1 Transport may be withdrawn for serious misbehaviour after a warning to parents.

8. POST-16 TRANSPORT
8.1 Students aged 16 to 18 may buy a discounted travel pass; there is no free entitlement.

PUBLICATION AND EARLIER VERSIONS
A copy of this document is published on the organisation's website. Earlier versions are archived and remain available for reference, together with every amendment and the date from which it applies.

POLICY FOR 2025/26 ACADEMIC YEAR — additional rule 2.3
2.3 A child aged 8 to 11 from a Low-income Family is entitled to free transport to any of their three nearest suitable schools that lies more than 2 miles but not more than 6 miles from home.

APPLICATION HT-2025-4492 — received 12 May 2025, for September 2025
Pupil: Rhys Adebayo, aged 9 on 1 September 2025.
Family status: Rhys receives free school meals.
Nearest suitable school: St Anselm's Primary, 2.6 miles by walking route.
School attended: Brookfield Primary, the second-nearest suitable school, 4.1 miles by walking route.
Transport officer's draft: "Nearest school is inside 3 miles — not entitled; offer spare seat."
instructions: Is the pupil entitled to free home-to-school transport for 2025/26?
card:
- entitled_under_8_rule: Primary pupils are measured against the 2-mile Walking Distance, and his Nearest Suitable School is 2.6 miles away, beyond it, so he is entitled under rule 2.1.
- entitled_low_income_rule: Rhys is 9, from a Low-income Family, and attends one of his three nearest suitable schools between 2 and 6 miles away, so rule 2.3 entitles him.
- entitled_nearest_school_only: Rule 2.3 entitles him to free transport only to St Anselm's, not to Brookfield.
- not_entitled: The low-income rule does not apply, and his Nearest Suitable School is within Walking Distance, so there is no entitlement.

BRINDLEFORD CITY COUNCIL — CONSTRUCTION SITE NOISE: CODE OF PRACTICE AND ENFORCEMENT POLICY

1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 "Permitted Hours" means the hours in which noisy work may be carried out.
1.2 "Noisy Work" means work audible at the boundary of any occupied property, including breakers, piling and angle grinders.
1.3 "Warning" means a written warning issued by an environmental health officer and recorded on the site file.
1.4 "Fixed Penalty" means a fixed penalty notice of £400.

2. PERMITTED HOURS
2.1 Monday to Friday: 08:00 to 18:00.
2.2 Saturday: 08:00 to 13:00.
2.3 Sundays and bank holidays: no Noisy Work.

3. ENFORCEMENT
3.1 A first breach of Permitted Hours results in a Warning.
3.2 A further breach within 6 months of a Warning results in a Fixed Penalty.
3.3 Persistent breaches may lead to a notice under section 60 of the Control of Pollution Act, specifying conditions for the site.

4. DUST
4.1 Sites must damp down dusty operations and sheet lorries.

5. DELIVERIES
5.1 Deliveries by vehicles over 7.5 tonnes are not permitted before 07:30.

6. EXEMPTIONS
6.1 Emergency work to make a structure safe may be carried out at any time; the contractor must notify the Council within 24 hours.

7. COMMUNITY LIAISON
7.1 Sites expected to last more than three months must write to neighbours with a contact number before work begins.

8. MONITORING
8.1 Officers may install noise monitors at site boundaries. Readings are shared with the contractor.

EQUALITY
The organisation applies this document fairly and consistently, without discrimination on the basis of any protected characteristic, and monitors its use to identify any unintended effects.

CONFIDENTIALITY OF RECORDS
Case files and correspondence relating to decisions under this document are kept confidential and are disclosed only to those who need them to make or review a decision, or where the law requires.

CODE UPDATE — effective 1 June 2025
U1. Paragraph 2.2 is replaced: "Saturday: 09:00 to 13:00."
U2. Paragraphs 2.1, 2.3 and section 3 are unchanged.

SITE FILE — 40 Marlowe Street (contractor: Tanfield Build Ltd)
• 3 February 2025: Warning issued for grinding at 18:40 on a weekday.
• Complaint received: hydraulic breaker in use at 08:30 on Saturday 14 June 2025, breaking out the old patio.
• Officer's visit on the day confirmed the breaker was running and audible at the neighbouring houses.
• No emergency was claimed.
• Site manager's statement: "We've always been allowed to start at eight on Saturdays."
instructions: What enforcement step should the environmental health officer take?
card:
- serve_section_60_notice: With a weekday breach in February and a Saturday breach in June, the contractor's breaches are persistent, so a section 60 notice must be served on the site.
- no_breach: The works took place within the Permitted Hours for a Saturday, so there was no breach.
- issue_warning: Each breach of the Code is dealt with on its own, and this is the site's first breach of Saturday hours, so a Warning is the correct first step.
- issue_fixed_penalty: Saturday work now starts at 09:00, so the 08:30 breaker was a breach, and it came within 6 months of the February Warning: a Fixed Penalty follows.

GARSTON DISTRICT COUNCIL — BUILDING CONTROL CHARGES SCHEME

1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 "Plan Charge" means the charge for checking plans submitted with a full plans application.
1.2 "Inspection Charge" means the charge for site inspections during the work, paid in advance with the application.
1.3 "Plan Check" means the Council's examination of the plans; it is complete when a decision notice or a request for amended plans is sent.
1.4 "Administration Fee" means the Council's fee for processing a withdrawal.

2. CHARGES
2.1 Charges are set out in Table A and depend on the type and size of the work.
2.2 VAT is included in all charges.

3. WITHDRAWALS AND REFUNDS
3.1 If an application is withdrawn before the Plan Check has started, both charges are refunded in full.
3.2 If an application is withdrawn after the Plan Check is complete but before the first inspection, the Inspection Charge is refunded less an Administration Fee of £50. The Plan Charge is not refunded.
3.3 After the first inspection, refunds are at the Council's discretion.

4. REGULARISATION
4.1 Applications for work already carried out are charged at 150% of the standard charge.

5. PAYMENT
5.1 Charges are payable on submission. Applications are not validated until payment clears.

6. DISPUTES
6.1 Disputes about charges are referred to the Head of Building Control.

7. LAPSED APPLICATIONS
7.1 Applications on which no work has started within three years lapse; charges are not refunded.

8. PAYMENT METHODS
8.1 Refunds are made to the card or account used for payment within 20 working days.

9. PARTIAL WITHDRAWAL
9.1 Where only part of the proposed work is withdrawn, charges are recalculated on the remaining work.

WAIVER
A failure or delay in enforcing any provision is not a waiver of it, and a waiver on one occasion does not apply to any other occasion or to any other provision.

CARNWORTH UNITARY COUNCIL — HOUSEHOLD LEVY: DISCOUNTS AND DISREGARDS

1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 "Levy Year" means 1 April to 31 March.
1.2 "Counted Adult" means a resident aged 18 or over who is not a Disregarded Person.
1.3 "Disregarded Person" means (a) a full-time student, (b) a resident care worker, or (c) a person with a severe mental impairment certified by a doctor.
1.4 "Band C Levy" means £1,840 for the 2025/26 Levy Year.

2. DISCOUNTS
2.1 Where a home has only one Counted Adult, the levy is reduced by 25%.
2.2 Where a home has no Counted Adults, the levy is reduced by 50%.
2.3 Discounts are applied from the date the circumstances begin.

3. EXEMPTIONS
3.1 Homes occupied only by full-time students are exempt.

4. REPORTING CHANGES
4.1 Residents must tell the Council of any change affecting a discount within 21 days.

5. PAYMENT
5.1 The levy is payable in ten monthly instalments from April.

6. APPEALS
6.1 Disputes about discounts may be appealed to the valuation tribunal.

7. EVIDENCE
7.1 Claims for a disregard must be supported by evidence, such as a student certificate, a care provider's letter or an apprenticeship agreement.

8. PENALTIES
8.1 Failing to report a change that ends a discount may lead to a £70 penalty.

9. BACKDATING
9.1 Discounts may be backdated up to six years where the circumstances are proved.

10. SECOND HOMES
10.1 Homes that are no one's main residence pay a premium of 100% of the levy.

ACCESSIBILITY

CARRADALE FOUNDATION — MERIT SCHOLARSHIP TERMS

1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 "Scholar" means a student holding a Carradale Merit Scholarship.
1.2 "Annual GPA" means the grade point average for the academic year just completed, on a 4.0 scale.
1.3 "Cumulative GPA" means the grade point average across all years completed.
1.4 "Review" means the committee's annual review of each Scholar, held in June.
1.5 "Entry Cohort" means the September in which the Scholar began their degree.

2. AWARD
2.1 The scholarship pays £6,000 a year towards tuition for up to four years.
2.2 Payments are made to the university in two instalments, in October and February.

3. CONTINUATION
3.1 To keep the scholarship, a Scholar must achieve an Annual GPA of at least 3.0 at each Review.
3.2 A Scholar who falls below that standard loses the scholarship from the next academic year. There is no probation period.
3.3 A Scholar who takes an approved leave of absence is reviewed on return.

4. CONDUCT
4.1 A Scholar found responsible for serious academic misconduct loses the scholarship immediately.

5. SERVICE
5.1 Scholars attend one Foundation mentoring event each year.

6. APPEALS
6.1 A Scholar may appeal a Review outcome on the ground of documented extenuating circumstances within 14 days.

7. LEAVE OF ABSENCE
7.1 A Scholar may take up to one year's approved leave; the scholarship is suspended, not lost, during leave.

8. TRANSFERS
8.1 A Scholar who changes degree programme within the same university keeps the scholarship if the committee approves.

9. CHANGES TO THESE TERMS
9.1 The trustees may amend these terms. An amendment applies to the Scholars it names, from the date it states.

1.3 "Early Retirement" means taking pension before Normal Pension Age, from age 55.
1.4 "Retirement Date" means the date the pension starts.

4. EARLY RETIREMENT
4.1 A member may take Early Retirement with the employer's consent or after leaving service.
4.2 The Accrued Pension is reduced by 4% for each year between the Retirement Date and Normal Pension Age, calculated pro rata for part years in complete months.
4.3 No reduction applies on ill-health retirement approved by the scheme doctor.

5. LUMP SUM
5.1 A member may exchange part of the pension for a tax-free lump sum at a rate of £12 for each £1 of pension given up.

6. INCREASES
6.1 Pensions in payment increase each April by inflation, up to 5%.

7. DEATH BENEFITS
7.1 A spouse or partner receives 50% of the member's pension after the member's death.

8. TRANSFERS
8.1 Members may transfer out up to one year before Normal Pension Age.

9. DEFERRED MEMBERS
9.1 A member who leaves service before Normal Pension Age becomes a deferred member; the Accrued Pension is revalued each year until it is paid.
9.2 Revaluation stops on the Retirement Date. In this case revaluation has already been applied in the Accrued Pension shown.

PLEDGEHOUSE — CREATOR TERMS OF USE

1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 "Campaign" means a fundraising page published by a creator with a funding target and deadline.
1.2 "All-or-Nothing" means a Campaign in which the creator receives funds only if the target is reached by the deadline.
1.3 "Pledge" means a backer's commitment, charged when the Campaign closes.
1.4 "Fees" means the 5% platform fee and 3% payment processing fee deducted from funds released.

2. CAMPAIGNS
2.1 All Campaigns are All-or-Nothing.
2.2 If an All-or-Nothing Campaign does not reach its target by the deadline, no Pledges are charged and backers owe nothing.
2.3 Deadlines may not be extended once a Campaign is live.

3. PROHIBITED CAMPAIGNS
3.1 Campaigns may not raise funds for financial products, weapons or political parties.

4. REWARDS
4.1 Creators must deliver promised rewards or refund backers who do not receive them.

5. PAYOUTS
5.1 Funds are released 14 days after a successful close, less Fees.

6. DISPUTES
6.1 Pledgehouse is not a party to agreements between creators and backers.

7. FEES
7.1 The platform fee is 5% and the payment processing fee is 3% of funds released.
7.2 No fee is charged when Pledges are not collected.

8. BACKER REFUNDS
8.1 Backers cannot cancel a Pledge in the last 48 hours of a Campaign.

9. CHANGES
9.1 Changes to these terms state the Campaigns to which they apply; a Campaign keeps the funding model chosen at launch.

COUNTERPARTS AND ELECTRONIC SIGNATURE
This document and any amendment to it may be signed electronically and in counterparts, each of which is an original and which together form one instrument.

CREATOR TERMS UPDATE — effective for Campaigns launched on or after 1 April 2025
U1. Clause 2.1 is replaced: "Creators choose, before launch, whether a Campaign is All-or-Nothing or Flexible Funding. In a Flexible Funding Campaign, Pledges are charged at the deadline and funds are released to the creator whether or not the target is reached."
U2. Clauses 2.2, 2.3 and 5.1 are unchanged.

Launched: 3 May 2025. Funding model selected at launch: Flexible Funding.

Creator's request, 1 July: "Please extend the deadline two weeks so we can hit 100%."
Support agent's draft: "Unfortunately you missed your target, so all pledges will be cancelled."
instructions: What should the platform do with the pledges when the campaign closes?
card:
- cancel_all_pledges: The Campaign did not reach its target by the deadline, and under its funding model no Pledges are charged.
- release_funds_less_fees: Under the April update this Flexible Funding Campaign pays out whether or not the target is met, so the £14,000 is released less Fees.
- release_70_percent_of_target: Flexible Funding releases money only in proportion to the target reached, so 70% of each Pledge is charged and passed to the creator less Fees.
- extend_deadline: A creator who is close to target may have the deadline extended by up to two weeks.

UNIVERSITY OF CASTLEMERE — ACCESS BURSARY SCHEME

1. DEFINITIONS
1.1 "Household Income" means the gross taxable income of the student's parents or partner for the previous tax year, as assessed by the student finance agency. It excludes child benefit and disability benefits.
1.2 "Entry Year" means the academic year in which the student first enrolled on the programme.
1.3 "Full Bursary" means £3,000 a year.

COUNTERPARTS AND ELECTRONIC SIGNATURE
This document and any amendment to it may be signed electronically and in counterparts, each of which is an original and which together form one instrument.

DATA PROTECTION
Personal information collected under this document is used only to administer it, is kept no longer than necessary, and may be shared with service providers who process it on the organisation's behalf. Individuals may ask for a copy of the information held about them.

2. BURSARY AMOUNTS (for Entry Years up to 2024/25)
2.1 Household Income of £25,000 or less: Full Bursary.
2.2 Household Income above £25,000: the Full Bursary is reduced by £1 for every £10 of income above £25,000, reaching nil at £55,000.

3. PAYMENT
3.1 Bursaries are paid in three instalments, in November, February and May, subject to attendance.

4. CONTINUING STUDENTS
4.1 A continuing student remains on the scheme that applied to their Entry Year, reassessed each year on current Household Income.

5. OTHER AWARDS
5.1 Students may also hold a subject scholarship; the two are not combined for any cap.

6. REPAYMENT
6.1 Students who withdraw repay any instalment paid for a term they did not attend.

7. EVIDENCE
7.1 The university relies on the Household Income figure assessed by the student finance agency, after removing the excluded benefits named in 1.1.

8. ROUNDING
8.1 Bursary amounts are rounded to the nearest pound.

9. CHANGES
9.1 New bursary amounts apply to students by Entry Year, as stated in the change.

BURSARY AMOUNTS — for Entry Year 2025/26 onwards
2A.1 Household Income of £30,000 or less: Full Bursary.
2A.2 Household Income above £30,000: the Full Bursary is reduced by £1 for every £10 of income above £30,000, reaching nil at £60,000.

STUDENT ASSESSMENT — 2025/26
Student: Farah Idowu, BA History. Entry Year: 2025/26 (first year).
Assessed household income reported by the agency: £40,000 gross, which includes £1,500 of child benefit.
No disability benefits. Attendance: full.
Student's question: "My friend in second year on the same income gets less — which rules do I come under?"
instructions: What bursary is the student entitled to for the year?
card:
- bursary_2150: Under the 2025/26 rules, Household Income of £38,500 is £8,500 over the £30,000 threshold, so £3,000 − £850 = £2,150.
- bursary_1650: Household Income of £38,500 is £13,500 over the £25,000 threshold, so £3,000 − £1,350 = £1,650.
- bursary_3000: A first-year student receives the Full Bursary before any reassessment.
- bursary_2000: Income of £40,000 is £10,000 over £30,000, so £3,000 − £1,000 = £2,000.
- bursary_1300: The bursary falls by £1 for every £5 of the £8,500 above £30,000, so £3,000 − £1,700 = £1,300.
